short: The most successful British heavy bomber of the Second World War, capable of carrying the heaviest ordnance of the conflict.
full:
Introduced in 1942, the Avro Lancaster was a four-engine heavy bomber that became the mainstay of the Royal Air Force's Bomber Command. Evolving from the unsuccessful twin-engine Manchester, the Lancaster was characterised by an enormous, unobstructed bomb bay that allowed it to carry massive payloads. It delivered the overwhelming majority of bombs dropped by the British during the night-time strategic bombing offensive that devastated Germany's cities and infrastructure.

The Lancaster's versatile design enabled it to carry specialized, oversized weapons that no other aircraft could lift, including the bouncing bombs used in the 1943 Dambusters raid and the enormous 22,000-pound Grand Slam earthquake bombs. Over seven thousand Lancasters were built, flying more than 150,000 sorties. Despite appalling loss rates among Bomber Command crews, the aircraft remained the backbone of British strategic air power until the end of the conflict.
